question: According to Mendel, when a tall pea plant ( TT ) is crossed with a short pea plant ( tt ), the F₁ offspring will be:
solution:
The correct answer is __**all tall (Tt)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• According to **Mendel's Laws of Inheritance**, when a **homozygous tall pea plant (TT)** is crossed with a **homozygous short pea plant (tt)**, it represents a **monohybrid cross**, which focuses on a single trait (stem height).
 
• During the process of **meiosis**, the parent plants produce gametes. The tall plant (**TT**) produces gametes that all carry the **T** allele, while the short plant (**tt**) produces gametes that all carry the **t** allele.
 
• In the **F1 (First Filial) generation**, the fusion of these gametes results in offspring that all have the **heterozygous genotype (Tt)**.
